pressure.p1: European companies, vendors, and investors now face a concrete demand: produce structured technical evidence — not policy statements — on AI deployment, procurement admissibility, and transaction exposure.
pressure.p2: Regulators, public buyers, financial institutions, and deal teams are not asking for more governance frameworks. They are asking for proof.
pressure.p3: The firms that can produce that proof on behalf of their clients — quickly, under their own name — will capture the mandate.

model.heading: How it works
model.artifactBody: A structured technical evidence artifact. Built from a client archetype — sector, jurisdiction, company size, AI surface. No client data ingested. No discovery sessions. Same input produces the same artifact shape. Delivered as a document your firm signs.
model.partnerBody: The partner deploys it under their letterhead. As the evidence layer beneath a legal opinion, a procurement mandate, a due diligence brief, or a board advisory. The artifact creates the factual base. The partner creates the legal interpretation.
model.doctrine: The artifact surfaces conditions. The lawyer names the law.

partners.heading: Built for boutique law firms
partners.subhead: White-label. Under your letterhead. No data-processing surface.
partners.p1: The artifact is built from a client archetype, not from client data. No client systems, contracts, records, or documents are accessed. No software is installed. No processing agreement is required. You receive a document. You sign it. You bill it.
partners.p2: Your clients are already receiving AI risk questions. Regulators, public buyers, financial institutions, and deal teams are creating pressure that legal advisors cannot answer with frameworks alone. The firms that can answer those questions with structured technical evidence — under their own name — hold the advisory relationship.
partners.p3: The artifact is the evidence layer. Your interpretation is the legal opinion. That division of labor makes you more valuable to the client, not less.
partners.note: For boutique law firms only. Three questions. Response within 48 hours. First conversation is a scoping call — not a pitch.

case1.title: Employment audit
case1.situation: A mid-market company has deployed Microsoft Copilot across its workforce. An employment partner needs a structured technical evidence base before a works council consultation or a regulatory review arrives.
case1.produces: AI deployment map by business function. HR exposure signals. Evidence gaps in documentation. Escalation triggers for the partner's legal assessment.
case1.partnerLabel: What the partner does with it
case1.partner: Uses it as the evidence layer beneath an employment law opinion. Bills it as enhanced due diligence. The artifact creates the factual record; the partner names the obligation.
